lede: The week's sharpest decision comes Tuesday, August 11, when Telluride Town Council takes up third reading of the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code — a vote that would rewrite Land Use Code rules around historic review and landscaping to meet state fire-mitigation standards, with real consequences for what property owners can plant and maintain. Ridgway's council is also busy Wednesday with a public hearing on the Hyde Subdivision replatting and a joint work session on its draft Housing Action Plan. Meanwhile, the Open Space Commission walks the Bear Creek Trailhead Monday to look at a potential new trail alignment and restoration work, and the Mushroom Festival rolls into town midweek.

notable.stake: Third-reading vote could rewrite landscaping and historic-review rules valley-wide.
Public hearing on Hyde Subdivision replatting plus housing-plan work session open for input.
County energy code update would revise building standards for new construction and major renovations.
